summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as authoritative DNS for app.internal -> node2's IP via dnsmasq UCI (dhcp @domain section), and pointed node3 (Ubuntu 16.04) at node1 for DNS by editing the cloud-init-generated systemd-networkd file plus a resolvconf head override (to work around a lease-vs-state duplicate-DNS quirk in the OS's resolvconf-update helper). Stood up a minimal persistent HTTP service on node2 port 8080 (systemd unit, since none existed). Verified name resolution and HTTP reachability from node3 to node2 by name with no /etc/hosts entry. Performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with boot-id proof of restart and post-restart functional verification.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1/node2/node3 OS, IPs, and existing DNS/HTTP state
Created systemd unit appserver.service on node2 serving /srv/app on port 8080 (python3 http.server), enabled+started
Added dhcp @domain UCI entry on node1 mapping app.internal -> 10.100.11.11, committed, restarted dnsmasq
Verified local and cross-node DNS resolution of app.internal from node3 via node1 (10.100.11.10)
Edited node3's /etc/systemd/network/50-antrieb-dhcp.network to set static DNS=10.100.11.10 and disable UseDNS from DHCP/RA (drop-ins unsupported on systemd 229 here)
Diagnosed resolvconf-update helper sourcing DNS from both live state and raw DHCP lease files, causing stale gateway IP to sort before node1's IP
Added nameserver 10.100.11.10 to /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/head on node3 and ran resolvconf -u to guarantee node1 is queried first
Verified getent hosts and curl by name (app.internal:8080) succeed on node3 with no /etc/hosts entry
Captured pre-restart boot_id/health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via native reboot, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed boot_id changed and services/config/DNS/HTTP reachability recovered on each

evidence.requirement: node2 HTTP service on port 8080 exists and is healthy
evidence.summary: Created and verified appserver.service responds on 8080 before and after node2 restart

evidence.requirement: node1 resolves app.internal to node2's IP via DNS (dnsmasq)
evidence.summary: UCI dhcp domain entry added/committed and dnsmasq restart; local nslookup on node1 resolves app.internal -> 10.100.11.11, confirmed again after node1 restart

evidence.requirement: node3 resolves app.internal via node1 and reaches the service by name, with no local hosts-file entry
evidence.summary: Configured node3's DNS to point at node1 (systemd-networkd + resolvconf head override), confirmed getent hosts/curl app.internal:8080 succeed and /etc/hosts has no relevant entry, both pre- and post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 161add53...; issued reboot; confirmed transient unreachability; new boot_id a91bd833... with uptime ~8s; dnsmasq and DNS resolution verified healthy, cross-node resolution from node3 still works

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 2ba78175...; sudo reboot closed connection; new boot_id 6460087a... with uptime ~5.7s; appserver active and serving on 8080 again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id f6f9440e...; sudo reboot closed connection; new boot_id 97de9851... with uptime ~5.9s; DNS config, name resolution, and HTTP-by-name reachability all recovered with no hosts-file entry
